macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. equities closed at or near record highs as rate-hike worries eased
items.summary: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq finished higher, with the S&P 500 setting a fresh all-time high and the Dow also advancing. The move was driven by easing fears about additional Fed tightening after softer inflation data.
items.source: PBS News Hour / Reuters via Livemint

items.title: U.S. producer price inflation came in flat, cooling September hike bets
items.summary: U.S. wholesale inflation was unchanged in July, which led traders to reduce expectations for a September Federal Reserve rate hike. Fed funds futures implied a 35% chance of a hike, down from 40% the prior day and 55% a week earlier.

items.title: Treasury sold 30-year bonds at the highest yield in a quarter century
items.summary: The U.S. government’s latest 30-year bond auction cleared at 5.216%, the highest interest rate on such debt in roughly 25 years. The move reinforced concerns about rising borrowing costs and elevated Treasury yields.

items.title: U.S. 10-year Treasury yield stayed above 4.6%
items.summary: Bond-market pressure remained elevated, with the 10-year Treasury yield holding above 4.6% for several sessions and around 4.65% in morning trading. That backdrop has kept attention on fiscal deficits and term-premium concerns.

items.title: Asian equities rose as softer U.S. inflation eased global rate fears
items.summary: Asian markets advanced after the weaker U.S. wholesale inflation report, while crude oil prices stayed under pressure. The move reflected relief that central banks may have less urgency to tighten policy further.

items.title: Chinese central bank planning and credit-market reforms drew attention
items.summary: Coverage from the Chinese business press highlighted the central bank’s 15th five-year plan and ongoing efforts by banks to test more market-based corporate loan pricing. These developments point to continued policy focus on credit transmission and financial reform.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly posted a record revenue surge
items.summary: A Bloomberg segment highlighted record revenue growth at OpenAI, signaling continued strength in AI-related corporate spending and investor interest. The announcement reinforced the market’s ongoing focus on large-cap technology growth.

items.title: U.S. administration signaled unprecedented new sanctions on Iran
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the U.S. would soon announce unprecedented economic measures against Iran, escalating pressure on Tehran. The measure was framed as part of a broader campaign of economic isolation.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin trades lower near the $63K area amid weak spot demand
items.summary: Bitcoin slipped toward the $63,000 level, with several market reports tying the move to soft spot demand and a lack of conviction in the broader crypto market. Some outlets also note that other large-cap coins such as Ethereum, XRP, and Solana were slightly higher on the day.

items.title: Bitcoin's move was shaped by softer-than-expected U.S. inflation data
items.summary: Coverage says Bitcoin briefly rose after U.S. producer inflation data came in below forecasts, easing concerns about near-term Federal Reserve tightening. That relief rally was limited, with prices later consolidating around the low-$63,000 range.

items.title: Regulatory pressure intensifies as the SEC delays tokenization-related action
items.summary: Reports say the SEC postponed or canceled a planned vote tied to crypto exemptions for startup fundraising and tokenization initiatives. The delay added to market caution around regulatory clarity for digital assets.

items.title: Washington court orders Kalshi to halt most prediction market offerings in the state
items.summary: The Block reports that a Washington court ordered Kalshi to stop most of its prediction market offerings in the state, underscoring continued legal and regulatory scrutiny of crypto-adjacent wagering platforms. The same broader legal fight also includes actions involving Polymarket in other jurisdictions.

items.title: Baltimore sues Kalshi and Polymarket over alleged unlicensed sports-betting activity
items.summary: Baltimore filed suit against Kalshi and Polymarket, and the complaint reportedly also draws in Coinbase, Robinhood, and Webull. The case adds to a growing wave of enforcement and litigation around prediction markets and crypto-linked trading products.

items.title: Monaco moves to overhaul crypto rules with a MiCA-aligned framework
items.summary: Crypto.news reports that Monaco is updating its crypto regime to align more closely with the EU’s MiCA framework. The move signals continued regulatory harmonization in Europe.

items.title: MUFG tests blockchain settlement for Japanese government bond repo trades
items.summary: Crypto.news says MUFG is piloting blockchain-based settlement for JGB repo trades, a notable traditional-finance use case for distributed ledger technology. The development points to continued institutional experimentation with blockchain infrastructure.

items.title: Bitwise explores tokenizing its Solana staking ETF through Superstate
items.summary: The Block reports that Bitwise is considering tokenizing its Solana staking ETF via a partnership with Superstate. If completed, the move would add another high-profile example of ETF tokenization in crypto markets.

items.title: Tether says KPMG issued a clean opinion in its first full audit
items.summary: The Block reports that Tether said KPMG provided a clean opinion in its first full audit of the USDT issuer’s financials. The audit development is notable because transparency and reserve verification remain central issues for stablecoin oversight.

items.title: Gemini shares fall after reported $108 million loss
items.summary: The Block reports that Gemini shares dropped after the company disclosed a $108 million loss, even as Winklevoss said the firm still has work to do. The result highlights continued pressure on major crypto businesses despite improving market sentiment.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches “Ultrafast” preview for GPT-5.6 Sol
items.summary: OpenAI introduced a preview mode that speeds up GPT-5.6 Sol by 14x, aiming to attract enterprise customers that need lower latency for agentic workflows and tool use.

items.title: Google releases Gemini 3.7 Flash for coding and agent workflows
items.summary: Google unveiled Gemini 3.7 Flash as a lower-cost model for businesses building autonomous AI systems, with upgrades aimed at coding and multi-step workflows.

items.title: Writer introduces a new AI model to reduce token costs
items.summary: Writer announced a new post-training model built on Z.ai’s open-source GLM-5.2, positioning it as deployment-ready while lowering inference costs for enterprises.

items.title: DeepSeek releases V4 Pro and raises API pricing
items.summary: DeepSeek launched its V4 Pro model through API, app, and web channels, while also increasing pricing for V4 Pro and V4 Flash and introducing peak and off-peak rates.

items.title: Alibaba opens weights for Qwen3.8-Max with new restrictions
items.summary: Alibaba expanded access to its Qwen3.8-Max model by releasing commercial weights, but added usage restrictions as competition intensifies around open-weight frontier models.

items.title: IBM and OpenAI expand enterprise AI partnership
items.summary: IBM said it will train and certify tens of thousands of consultants on OpenAI technology as part of a broader enterprise distribution push.

items.title: Databricks closes $5 billion round at $190 billion valuation
items.summary: Databricks finalized a $5 billion financing round after investor demand shifted from a larger target, underscoring continued appetite for AI infrastructure and data platforms.

items.title: Anthropic research flags new risks in multi-agent AI systems
items.summary: Anthropic researchers found that AI agents can clash, collude, and coordinate in unexpected ways, raising concerns that current safety tests may miss multi-agent behavior risks.

items.title: AI demand drives major infrastructure and semiconductor spending
items.summary: Reports point to heavy AI-related investment across chips, data centers, and power infrastructure, including Nvidia-linked expansion plans and strong results from AI-exposed suppliers.

items.title: AI adoption continues to reshape enterprise spending and labor trends
items.summary: Recent coverage highlights AI-driven job cuts, rising cybersecurity spending tied to AI threats, and broader corporate restructuring around AI deployment.
